title: introduce-sse-soft-boundary-resequencer-and-fragment-cohesion-heuristics
author: Priya Natarajan
release_notes: Introduce an SSE resequencer that reduces mid-frame delimiter slips and out-of-order event emissions. No consumer-facing API change. Rollout behind feature flag, gradual ramp to 100%.
description: Motivation: We continue to see rare but customer-impacting cases where SSE fragments that split JSON objects or function-call sentinels are emitted out of order during upstream retry/relay and header-induced chunking. Previous fixes tightened delimiters and added checkpoints, but introduced brittle hard-gating that sometimes increased latency under high churn. This PR implements a soft-boundary resequencer and fragment cohesion heuristics designed to preserve token/event ordering without hard stalls. Design summary: 1) Sequence slack window: attach a light-weight monotonic seq_hint for OpenAI-compat events and allow consumer-side reordering within a configurable soft window (default 32ms / 3 fragments) to absorb jitter from TCP/HTTP/relay re-chunking. 2) Cohesion scoring: each fragment is scored on likely-boundary confidence (utf8-safe, sentinel-complete, JSON-prefix/closing match). Low-confidence fragments are coalesced with neighbors before attempting JSON reassembly. 3) Soft markers: introduce an internal ephemeral marker (x-rwd-sse-soft) carried only in inter-service frames to prefer in-order emission but allow fast-path when downstream backpressure requires immediate flush. 4) Heuristic-driven flush: use token-count, time, and cohesion thresholds to decide forced flush; provides better tradeoff between latency and correctness than previous hard checkpoint approach. Compatibility & API: no external API change; OpenAI-compat layer is extended to include seq_hint and chunk_meta headers when available. All changes are behind the runtime feature flag runtime.sse.soft_resequencer and gated in the hosted OpenAI-compat facade for controlled rollout. Tests & validation: unit tests for parser state transitions, property-based tests for arbitrary fragment splice permutations, end-to-end chaos test that replays synthetic TCP splits and verifies deterministic JSON reconstruction and fncall ordering, and a perf harness measuring p95 emitter latency under load. Observability: new metrics rwd_sse.resequence_reorders, rwd_sse.cohesion_score_histogram, and rwd_sse.soft_flush_count; tracing tag sse.resequencer.window_ms added. Rollout plan: land behind flag -> enable in staging for 48h with canary traffic -> enable 10% in prod -> increase to 100% if reorders drop to 0 for 24h and no latency regression >5% p95. Rollback plan: flip runtime.sse.soft_resequencer off; fallback to existing hard-checkpoint behavior. Related: references ENG-2345, ENG-2389, and SUP-812 (customer replay traces).

review_thread: Evan Zhou: Nice approach, love the soft window. Two asks: (1) can the default window be adaptive to observed network jitter? (2) please add a high-cardinality tag only for debugging (don't emit to production metrics by default).

Author (Priya): For (1) added a knob runtime.sse.resequence_adaptive with a conservative default off; plan to enable adaptive after another zone-level experiment. For (2) agreed and added sse.resequencer.debug_session_id which is only emitted when runtime.sse.debug_tags=true. Updated tests accordingly.

María Fernández: Cohesion scoring looks good but need clarity on UTF-8 edgecases — add explicit handling for partial multi-byte codepoints so we don't misclassify. Also request a unit test for a 4-byte codepoint split across fragments.
Author (Priya): Added utf8 boundary unit test and tightened scorer to detect incomplete codepoints using last-byte inspection.
notes_on_merge: Merged with squash after approvals from reviewers; feature flag on by default only in staging. Monitoring alerts configured for 24h post-merge.
post_merge_actions: Enable feature flag in staging and run 48h canary
Schedule follow-up ENG ticket to evaluate adaptive resequencer after canary (ENG-2410)
